title: Record actual preparation start
purpose: Record or correct the actual start used as preparation evidence and for holding-time evaluation.
summary: Record or correct the actual time preparation started. It is preparation evidence and is used for holding-time clocks.

tasks.title: Record the start
steps: Enter the actual start in laboratory local time.

good_to_know: The start cannot be before the collection of a linked sample, or after the recorded completion.
Once a submitted or approved result relies on this preparation, the start cannot change. A reviewer can return submitted work first.
Entered draft results are not rewritten when the start changes.

sections.title: Context and field
paragraphs: Active internal staff with a laboratory role can read this workspace. Analysts can create and change preparation work. An admin has operational analyst access; a client account or superuser status alone does not grant it.
The Preparation panel displays Batch, Preparation method, Matrix and Actual start. Existing start is prefilled.

items.label: Preparation start
items.description: Required actual date and time in the laboratory time zone. It cannot exceed the server clock by more than two minutes, precede a linked sample or QC parent collection (collection end for composites), follow an existing completion, or follow existing preparation QC analysis.

items.label: Save preparation start
items.description: Saves the event and an attributed before/after audit event. The page checks that the batch has not changed since the form opened; reload a stale form and reconcile the displayed record. Membership may be closed.

items.label: Cancel
items.description: Returns to the preparation batch without saving.

sections.title: Submitted and historical work
paragraphs: Any submitted or approved revision linked to this preparation blocks a start change. A reviewer can return submitted work first; approved work requires reanalysis with a new batch/preparation and reason. Draft revisions are not rewritten when the start changes and must be entered again before submission so their evidence agrees. Existing original revisions remain preserved.
